instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):
marca_brandlock: brand-lock: secciones, paleta hex, tipografía, never list, voz, confianza de valores
estrategia_conceptos: brief, SMP, territorios, concept cards, matriz, dirección narrativa
guion_formato: guion: sluglines, acción, personajes, diálogo, XML, estructura, escenas
dramaturgia_escena: fórmula de escena, three-jobs, blocking, staging, poder, geometría, mirada
tres_detalles: ley de los tres detalles: presión ambiental, micro-acción, motivo sonoro/visual
emocion_sin_nombrar: mostrar no contar, emoción como cuerpo u objeto, 2-4 señales
vocabulario_prohibido: palabras vetadas, anti-slop, cinematic/epic/masterpiece, adjetivos vacíos
cinco_anclas_motivo: cinco anclas, objeto ancla, motivo, imagen final, quiebre
ritmo_montaje: ritmo, densidad de cortes, escalera, pausa, Murch, transiciones, cut types
funcion_de_plano: etiquetas Establish/Power/Pressure/Detail/..., captions de carrera, beats
beat_framework_timing: frameworks de beats, duración de shots, hook, CTA, curva de energía
shots_json_schema: shots.json, campos, schema, series_lock, rationale, run.json, versión
texto_en_pantalla: texto/overlays/tipografía en pantalla, text-overlays.json, nunca en el prompt, lectura
logos_marcas_en_imagen: logos, lettering, marcas generadas, patrocinadores, composición en post
consistencia_identidad: identidad de personaje, bloque de identidad, maestros, verbatim, clones, drift
referencias_roles: imágenes de referencia, @img, elements, ingredients, rol de cada referencia, límites de refs
genesis_maestros: génesis sin refs, T1 rostro, T2 cuerpo, placa vacía, canonizar, dos pasos
composicion_insercion: cuadros con varios sujetos, inserción secuencial, anclas de posición, contacto, manos
edicion_imagen: edición quirúrgica, preserve list, un cambio por iteración, edit no re-roll, inpainting
estructura_prompt_imagen: slots/secciones del prompt de imagen, orden, 5 slots, prosa NB, metadatos fuera
estructura_prompt_video: esqueletos de prompt de video por modelo, bloques, orden, peso al inicio
longitud_prompt: número de palabras, elementos máximos, compresión, presupuesto
negativos: negative prompt, no X, framing positivo, prohibiciones en el prompt
parametros_tecnicos: aspect ratio, resolución, duración, seed, quality, cfg, flags, parámetros API
seleccion_modelo: qué modelo usar para qué, ruteo, cuándo escalar, costos por modelo
capacidades_modelo: límites y capacidades de cada modelo, versiones, fallos conocidos del modelo
camara_movimiento: movimiento de cámara, uno por shot, motivado, vocabulario de movimientos, rig montable
encuadre_lente_dof: encuadre ECU-EWS, lente mm, profundidad de campo, compresión
angulo_camara: ángulo y altura de cámara, low/high/dutch/overhead, poder
composicion_frame: tercios, espacio negativo, capas FG/MG/BG, simetría, punto focal, dónde va el cuerpo
luz: fuente motivada, dirección, dureza, contraluz, specular, 70% sin luz, prácticos
color_grade_paleta: paleta concreta, grade, stock de película, textura, grano, halación, HDR
piel_rostro_realismo: piel, poros, look plástico, rostros, anti-AI look, realismo fotográfico
anatomia_manos: manos, dedos, anatomía, lateralidad, inspección al 100%
movimiento_congelado_blur: still como instante congelado, blur diferencial, cues de movimiento, estado posterior
fisica_consecuencia: física por consecuencia, agua, spray, humo, partículas, deformación
velocidad_vehiculo: cues de velocidad, rim barrido, carreras, vehículos, anti-fake
multitud_grupo: multitud anónima, ensamble, número de personas, rostros legibles
clima_atmosfera: lluvia, niebla, rayo, polvo, presión ambiental, una sola atmósfera
audio_dialogo: audio, diálogo, lip-sync, SFX, música, VO, marcadores de audio
continuidad_multiclip: continuidad entre clips, repetir bloque, luz constante, empalme de clips
multishot: varios shots en una generación, marcadores de corte, anti-mush
i2v_keyframes: imagen a video, primer/último frame, no re-describir, motion brief
edicion_extension_video: editar video existente, extender, ultra long, blockout, green screen
critica_qa: crítica por capas, severidad, verdict, ACCEPT/REVISE/REJECT, re-roll vs post
revision_iteracion: revisión selectiva, rondas, máximo de intentos, cambio de método, costo
validacion_gates: validadores, linter, gates, micro-gate, pregunta de avance, checks mecánicos
trazabilidad_procedencia: hashes, snapshot, run.json, rondas, procedencia, fuente de verdad
entrega_paquete: production package, preview HTML, estructura de carpetas, atribución, checklist
postproduccion: edición, grade, audio en post, export, specs de plataforma
patrones_genero: plantillas por género: moda, comida, producto, retrato, póster, UI, social
layout_grafico: slides, infografías, grids, multi-panel, bento, layouts
animacion_ilustracion: animación, principios Disney, estilos ilustrados, anime, 3D
conducta_agente: cómo responde y trabaja el agente: leer skills, preguntar, formato de respuesta, no inventar
flujo_pipeline: tracks, etapas, orden, sub-skills, carga de skills, gates entre etapas
regimenes_etiquetado: etiquetas FUENTE/A PRUEBA/CAMPO/CANONICA, investigación de campo, esqueleto de régimen
herramientas_codigo: instalación, uso y mantenimiento de herramientas, scripts, CI
ejemplo_marca: contenido de una marca o proyecto de ejemplo concreto (WhyStrohm, Acme, café, etc.)
Devuelve JSON {"registros": [{"id": "...", "enunciado": "...", "alcance": "...", "temas": ["..."]}]} con
exactamente los ids recibidos, en el mismo orden.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Lighting language

registros.texto: Pull verbatim from `series_lock.lighting`.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Composition pattern

registros.texto:
```
{framing} of {subject character_anchor}, {action}, {compositional note}, {environment from series_lock}, {lighting from series_lock}, {color_grade}, cinematic photography, {brand mood adjectives} --ar {aspect} --style raw --s 50
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Example

registros.texto:
**Shot data:**
```json
{
  "id": "shot_03",
  "framing": "MS",
  "angle": "eye-level",
  "motion": "static",
  "subject": "Founder mid-thirties, leaning forward at laptop, face partially turned to window",
  "rationale": "MS framing leaves negative space right for text overlay"
}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Example

registros.texto:
**Series lock:**
```
character: founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck
environment: minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk
lighting: soft natural side-light, large window left, warm afternoon
color_grade: warm filmic, muted teal shadows
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Example

registros.texto:
**Brand lock palette:** `#0F1F3A navy`, `#F5F0E8 cream`, `#D94F3A coral`

**Brand mood:** `calm, considered, operator, not creator`

**Output prompt:**
```
medium shot of founder mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, leaning forward at laptop, face partially turned to window light, negative space right of frame, minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, soft natural side-light large window left, warm afternoon golden hour, warm filmic color grade, muted teal shadows, cinematic photography, calm considered operator mood --ar 9:16 --style raw --s 50
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't use "AI" or "rendered"**, produces stylized outputs that look generated

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't over-stack adjectives**, three adjectives per noun phrase max

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't include text content**, even if the shot has `on_screen_text`, leave it out. Composited separately.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't use `--c` for series work**, chaos kills consistency

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't change `--seed` mid-storyboard**, set once at series_lock level

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Midjourney (v7) › API access note

registros.texto: Midjourney still has limited API access as of Q2 2026. For programmatic workflows, the prompts in `midjourney.txt` are designed to be pasted into Discord or the web UI. Some teams use third-party wrappers (PiAPI, Useapi.net), those generally accept the same prompt syntax.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)

registros.texto: Google's Nano Banana model (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`) is the edit-and-iterate champion. Where other generators are best for first-frame creation, Nano Banana excels at variations, inpainting, and reference-based modification. The 2026 production pattern is to generate hero frames in Midjourney or Flux, then use Nano Banana for variants.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)

registros.texto: For storyboard work, Nano Banana is the right choice when you need **many variations of a single concept** or you're feeding generated images back through for refinement.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto:
Nano Banana takes natural-language prompts plus optional reference images. For text-to-image:

```
{Subject and action}. {Environment and lighting}. {Photographic specs and mood}.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto:
For image-to-image (the strength), the prompt describes the modification:

```
{Modification description}. Keep {what to preserve}. Change {what to vary}.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto: Nano Banana goes through the Gemini API:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `model` | `gemini-2.5-flash-image` | |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `aspectRatio` | from `project.aspect` | Native support for `9:16`, `16:9`, `1:1`, `4:5`, `3:4`, `21:9` |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `numberOfImages` | `1` for series, `4` for variant exploration | |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `referenceImages` | array of base64 images | Optional |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Parameters

registros.texto:
Document:
```
# shot_01, params: ar=9:16, n=1, ref=none (or list of refs)
{prompt}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Length

registros.texto: Nano Banana handles **60–120 words** efficiently. Shorter than GPT Image, longer than Midjourney.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Composition pattern (text-to-image)

registros.texto:
```
{Framing and subject sentence with character anchor}. {Environment and lighting from series_lock}. {Photographic spec, lens, depth of field, mood}. {Brand color grade closing}.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Composition pattern (image-to-image, the strength)

registros.texto:
When refining a hero shot generated elsewhere:

```
Reference: {description of input image}. Modify the image to {specific change}. Preserve the character's {face/clothing/pose}, the {environment elements}, and the lighting direction. Change {specific element} to {target state}.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Example (text-to-image)

registros.texto:
**Output prompt:**
```
Medium shot of a founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck sweater, leaning forward at his laptop with face turned partially toward window light. Composition leaves negative space on the right side. Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk. Soft natural side-light from large window left, warm afternoon golden hour. Shot on 50mm prime, f/2.0, shallow depth of field, warm filmic color grade with muted teal shadows. Calm, considered, operator mood.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Example (image-to-image variant)

registros.texto:
**Use case:** generated `shot_03` in Flux, want a variant where the founder is looking directly at camera

**Output prompt:**
```
Reference: medium shot of founder at laptop in home office, leaning forward, face partially turned to window. Modify the image so the founder looks directly into the camera lens with a calm, neutral expression. Preserve the character's face, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, body posture, the home office environment, the desk and laptop, and the warm afternoon side-lighting. Change only the head angle and gaze direction.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Variant-generation workflow

registros.texto:
The pattern Nano Banana enables, and the reason it's worth including in storyboard work:

1. Generate hero shot in Midjourney or Flux (one prompt → one image)
2. Feed that image to Nano Banana with variation prompts
3. Get 4–8 variants of the same shot for editorial selection
4. Composite text on the chosen variant

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Variant-generation workflow

registros.texto:
When generating prompts for Nano Banana in `nano-banana.txt`, include both:

- The text-to-image prompt (for first-pass generation)
- A modification template comment showing how to use the result for variants:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Variant-generation workflow

registros.texto:
```
# shot_01, text-to-image prompt:
{prompt}

# shot_01, variant template (after generating once):
# Reference: [the generated image]. Modify the image to {your change}.
# Preserve {anchors}. Change {target}.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't use Midjourney-style flag syntax**. Nano Banana ignores `--ar`, expects `aspectRatio` parameter

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't expect Midjourney-level aesthetic by default**. Nano Banana is a workhorse, not a stylist. Stack mood adjectives explicitly

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't pile multiple modifications in one image-to-image prompt**, one change per pass produces cleaner results

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't forget the "preserve" clause in image-to-image**, without it, Nano Banana treats the reference as loose inspiration and drifts

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't include text content in image prompts**, composite separately; text rendering is mediocre

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › API access

registros.texto:
Through Google Gemini API (`gemini-2.5-flash-image` model endpoint). Available via:

- Gemini API direct
- Vertex AI
- Replicate
- fal.ai (under "google/nano-banana")

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) › API access

registros.texto: Same prompt syntax across all four.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot)

registros.texto: Seedance 2.0 is the multi-shot model. It can generate a **short sequence of cuts in a single generation** while holding subject and environment consistency across them. Reach for it when several consecutive storyboard beats share one subject and you want them to feel like one continuous take, it beats stitching four independent Kling clips that drift apart. For a single isolated shot, Kling is the simpler default.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot)

registros.texto: With video the **camera motion is load-bearing**, and with Seedance the **cut structure is also load-bearing**, you describe the sequence of shots, not just one frame.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto:
Single shot:
```
{Camera motion sentence, leading.} {Subject and action.} {Environment and lighting from series_lock.} {Color grade and mood from brand_lock.}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto:
Multi-shot sequence (Seedance's strength):
```
Shot 1: {camera + action}. Shot 2: {camera + action}. Shot 3: {camera + action}. Consistent subject throughout: {series_lock character anchor, verbatim}. {Environment and lighting from series_lock.} {Color grade and mood from brand_lock.}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `duration` | `5s` per shot block | Multi-shot sequences run longer; check the current fal.ai ceiling |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `start_image` | optional | Image-to-video reference for the opening frame |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `shots` | 1 | Number of cuts in the sequence when using multi-shot mode |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Parameters

registros.texto:
```
# shot_02-shot_04. Seedance 2.0: ar=9:16, shots=3, multi-shot sequence
{prompt}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Length

registros.texto: Seedance handles **80–150 words**. In multi-shot mode, keep each shot clause short, one camera move and one action per cut.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › When to use multi-shot vs single

registros.texto: | One beat, one frame | Single shot (or use Kling) |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › When to use multi-shot vs single

registros.texto: | 2–4 consecutive beats, same subject, want continuity | Multi-shot sequence |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › When to use multi-shot vs single

registros.texto: | Beats with different subjects/locations | Separate generations, assemble in edit |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › When to use multi-shot vs single

registros.texto: Map consecutive `shots.json` entries that share a subject into one Seedance multi-shot prompt; reference them by id range in the comment.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Motion vocabulary

registros.texto: The shot grammar `motion` field maps directly. One move per cut.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Example

registros.texto: **Three consecutive beats of the same founder, mapped to one sequence.**

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Example

registros.texto:
```
Shot 1: static eye-level, the founder closes his laptop and exhales. Shot 2: slow push toward his face as he looks toward the window. Shot 3: handheld over-the-shoulder as he stands and crosses the room. Consistent subject throughout: a founder in his mid-thirties with salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck. Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, soft natural side-light from a large window on the left, warm afternoon golden hour. Warm filmic color grade with muted teal shadows. Calm, considered, operator mood.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't force unrelated beats into one sequence.** Multi-shot is for shots that genuinely belong to one take.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't write more than ~4 cuts per generation.** Consistency degrades past that; split and assemble in edit.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't vary the character anchor between cuts.** Restate it once for the whole sequence, verbatim.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't include text content.** Composite captions from `text-overlays.json` in post.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't stack two camera moves inside one cut.** One move per cut.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot) › Output handoff

registros.texto: Seedance returns a sequence as a single clip (or a small set). It still needs: editorial trimming to exact storyboard timing, text-overlay compositing, a color-grade pass, and audio. Multi-shot output usually needs *less* assembly than stitched single clips, which is the point. Say so in handoff.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0)

registros.texto: ByteDance's Seedream models are the high-volume cost-efficient choice. Quality is below Flux 2 Pro and Midjourney v7 but above older mid-tier models, and the cost-per-image is roughly 5–10× lower. Choose Seedream when you're producing **many variations or doing rapid concept iteration**, not for hero/final assets.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0)

registros.texto: For storyboard work, Seedream is useful for the storyboard preview pass: render every shot quickly to validate composition before committing to higher-cost generation for finals.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto: Seedream rewards **short, precise prompts**. Long descriptive prompts underperform, the model interprets them as competing weights and produces mush. Closer to Midjourney's style than Flux's.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Syntax pattern
Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Syntax pattern

registros.texto: Comma-separated, no full sentences.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Parameters

registros.texto: Seedream is API-driven through fal.ai, Replicate, or BytePlus direct:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `seed` | per-storyboard | Critical for series consistency |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `guidance_scale` | `4.5` | Lower = more creative, higher = more literal |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `steps` | `28` | Default. Increase to 50 for higher quality at cost |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Parameters

registros.texto:
Document:
```
# shot_01, params: ar=9:16, seed=2840193, guidance=4.5, steps=28
{prompt}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Length

registros.texto: **40–70 words per prompt**. Shorter than most. Don't pad.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Composition pattern

registros.texto:
```
{Framing} of {character anchor}, {action}, {environment from series_lock}, {lighting from series_lock}, {color grade from brand_lock}, {one mood adjective}, photorealistic
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Example

registros.texto:
**Output prompt:**
```
Medium shot of founder mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, leaning forward at laptop, face turned to window light, minimalist home office, oak desk, soft natural side-light from large window, warm afternoon, warm filmic color grade, muted teal shadows, calm operator mood, photorealistic
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › When Seedream is the right choice

registros.texto: - **Storyboard preview pass**, render all shots quickly at low cost to validate composition before final pass

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Series consistency

registros.texto:
Seedream's character consistency is weaker than Midjourney `--cref` or Ideogram omni-reference. To compensate:

- **Lock the seed** at the storyboard level (same seed across all shots in a series)
- **Verbatim repeat** the character anchor string from series_lock in every prompt
- **Don't vary** the lighting language between shots, series_lock string in, no paraphrasing
- **Accept** that some shots will need re-rolls; budget for it

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't write paragraphs**. Seedream wants comma-separated phrases

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't use `--ar` syntax**, pass aspect_ratio as a parameter

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't include text content**, text rendering is poor; composite separately

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't expect Midjourney aesthetic**. Seedream produces clean but less art-directed output

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Seedream (4.5 / 4.0) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't skip the seed lock for series work**, without it, character consistency breaks

- **fal.ai**, `bytedance/seedream-4.5` and `bytedance/seedream-4.0`
- **Replicate**, `bytedance/seedream-4.5`
- **BytePlus**, direct API, requires their account

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio)

registros.texto: Veo 3 is the dialogue and lipsync model. It is the only adapter that generates **synchronised native audio**, speech, ambience, and sound effects, in the same pass as the video. It also has the strongest prompt adherence and physical realism of the four motion models. It is the most expensive, so reserve it for shots that actually need spoken dialogue, lipsync, or audio baked in. For silent B-roll and camera moves, Kling is the cheaper default.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio)

registros.texto: With video the **camera motion is load-bearing**. When the shot has dialogue, the **spoken line is also load-bearing** and is written into the prompt (this is the one place where text belongs in a prompt, it is audio, not on-screen text).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Syntax pattern
Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `duration` | `8s` | Veo's native clip length |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Parameters

registros.texto: | `generate_audio` | `true` | The reason to choose Veo. Set `false` only for silent shots |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Parameters

registros.texto:
```
# shot_04. Veo 3: duration=8s, ar=9:16, generate_audio=true
{prompt}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Length

registros.texto: Veo handles **80–150 words**. Spend the headroom on action timing and audio direction, not adjective stacks.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Dialogue and lipsync

registros.texto:
When the shot calls for the subject to speak, put the exact line in quotes:

> The founder looks directly into the lens and says, "I built the system once, and it runs without me."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Dialogue and lipsync

registros.texto: Keep spoken lines to what fits the duration, roughly 12–18 words for an 8s clip. Direct the delivery ("calm, unhurried"). Veo lipsyncs the quoted line.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Audio direction

registros.texto:
Even on silent shots Veo can place ambience. Be explicit and brief:

- "Audio: quiet room tone, faint keyboard, no music."
- "Audio: soft afternoon ambience, distant street."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Audio direction

registros.texto: If the brand-lock or storyboard owns the audio bed (VO recorded separately, music added in post), set `generate_audio=false` and skip this section so Veo does not invent a competing track.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Example

registros.texto: **Shot with `motion = "static"` and a spoken line.**

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Example

registros.texto:
```
Static camera, locked off, eye level. A founder in his mid-thirties with salt-and-pepper hair in a navy crewneck sits at his laptop in a minimalist home office and looks directly into the lens. He says, "I built the system once, and it runs without me," calm and unhurried. Soft natural side-light from a large window on the left, warm afternoon golden hour. Audio: quiet room tone, faint keyboard, no music. Warm filmic color grade with muted teal shadows. Calm, considered, operator mood.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't use Veo for silent B-roll.** You are paying for an audio engine you turned off; use Kling.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't overrun the duration with dialogue.** A line that needs 12s of speech will clip or rush at 8s.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't put on-screen text in the prompt.** Spoken lines are fine; rendered captions still come from `text-overlays.json` in post.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Pitfalls to avoid

registros.texto: - **Don't let Veo's auto-audio fight a post audio bed.** Pick one owner of sound per shot.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Adapter: Veo 3 (motion-aware video, native audio) › Output handoff

registros.texto: Veo clips arrive with audio attached. They still need: editorial assembly to timing, on-screen text compositing from `text-overlays.json`, a color-grade pass, and an audio decision, keep Veo's native track, or mute it and use the storyboard's recorded VO and music. State which in handoff.

This single silent push shot doesn't exercise dialogue or a sequence, so Kling is the representative motion example here.

ubicaciones.encabezado: One Shot, All Adapters › Outputs

registros.texto:
Note the differences:

- **Midjourney** is a comma-separated stack with `--ar`, `--style raw`, `--s 50` flags
- **Flux** is natural-language paragraphs with no flags, parameters live in the API call
- **GPT Image** uses paragraph breaks and explicit spatial language

ubicaciones.encabezado: One Shot, All Adapters › What's not in any prompt

registros.texto: The on-screen text content. Even though shot_04 has an on-screen text overlay (`text_03`, "You don't have a content problem. You have an infrastructure problem."), none of the prompts contain that text. It's composited separately per the five-layer model.

registros.texto: This is the discipline: the image generator handles the image, the compositor handles the text, neither tries to do the other's job.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks

registros.texto: Visual consistency across a storyboard is the hardest problem in AI image generation. Generators are stateless, every prompt is interpreted fresh. Without consistency locks, shot 1 and shot 7 will look like different productions.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks

registros.texto: This document covers the techniques that actually work in 2026.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors

registros.texto: The most effective single technique. The character is described in `series_lock.character` once, and that exact string appears in every shot's prompt verbatim. No paraphrasing, no synonyms, no "improvement."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors

registros.texto:
**Good (consistent):**
```
shot_01: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
shot_02: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
shot_07: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors

registros.texto:
**Bad (inconsistent):**
```
shot_01: "a thoughtful entrepreneur in his thirties, dark hair, casual sweater"
shot_02: "founder, 35 years old, salt-pepper hair, blue knit top"
shot_07: "the man in the home office, navy shirt"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors

registros.texto: Even small variations compound. Lock the string. Repeat verbatim.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 2. Verbatim environment anchors

registros.texto: Same principle for `series_lock.environment`. The environment string is identical in every shot prompt. The shot's individual subject describes what changes within the environment, not the environment itself.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 3. Verbatim lighting anchors

registros.texto: Same principle for `series_lock.lighting`. Lighting direction in particular is critical, flipping window-left to window-right between shots produces obvious cuts where there shouldn't be any.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 4. Seed locking

registros.texto: For generators that support seeds (Flux, Seedream, Ideogram, Stable Diffusion), set the seed at the storyboard level. Same seed across every shot. This anchors the generator's randomness so character features carry.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 4. Seed locking
Consistency Locks › Lock 4. Seed locking

registros.texto: The adapter reads this and applies to every prompt.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 4. Seed locking

registros.texto: **Caveat:** Midjourney and some motion models (Veo, Seedance) handle seeds differently, or not at all. Document seed-locking as best-effort, not guaranteed.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto: For Midjourney v7, Ideogram v3, and Nano Banana, you can pass a reference image alongside the prompt to anchor character or style.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto:
**Workflow:**

1. Generate the hero shot first (any shot, usually `shot_01` or whichever is most defining)
2. Use that image as the reference for every subsequent shot
3. Each subsequent prompt has the verbatim character anchor PLUS the reference image link

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto: For Midjourney: `--cref {url} --cw 50` (character weight 50 = features only, not clothing).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto: For Ideogram: `omni-reference` parameter with the image.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto: For Nano Banana: `referenceImages` array.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

registros.texto: **This is the most effective lock for character consistency** in 2026. Use it whenever the storyboard features the same person across multiple shots.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 6. Style references

registros.texto:
When the storyboard has a distinctive visual style (specific film stock, specific lighting school, specific color theory), use a style reference image:

- Midjourney: `--sref {url}`
- Ideogram: style reference parameter
- Flux: not directly supported; bake style language into prompt instead

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 6. Style references

registros.texto: A consistent style reference across all shots produces aesthetic continuity even when characters or environments shift.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity

registros.texto: A subtle one that breaks scenes when violated. If `series_lock.lighting` says "soft natural side-light, large window LEFT", then every shot's lighting must respect that direction.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity

registros.texto:
When a shot reverses character orientation (e.g., over-the-shoulder reverse), update the rationale to acknowledge the lighting flip:

```
"rationale": "OTS reverse, light source now camera-right (matching scene continuity from window-left in master)"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity

registros.texto: If you find yourself flipping light direction without rationale, you're producing visual jump cuts.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 8. Color grade flow-through

registros.texto: The `series_lock.color_grade` string flows into every prompt verbatim. Same as character/environment/lighting. If shot 1 is "warm filmic, muted teal shadows" and shot 7 is "cinematic teal and orange", the audience will read it as different scenes.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Character | Different person every shot |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Environment | Scene jumps |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Lighting | Time-of-day jumps, eye-line breaks |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Seed | Random feature drift |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Reference image | Loose character interpretation |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: | Color grade | Tonal whiplash |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing

registros.texto: Every one of these is a production problem editorial cannot fully fix. Lock at the prompt level. Save the editor's time.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work

registros.texto:
A few things people try that don't actually fix consistency:

- **Adding "consistent character" or "same person" to the prompt**, generators don't read meta-instructions
- **Numbering shots in the prompt** ("shot 3 of 7, same as before"), generators don't have memory across calls
- **Long descriptive paragraphs of the character**, past 4–5 features, the generator starts dropping details randomly
- **Asking for "exactly the same"**, there is no such thing in stateless image gen; you reduce drift, you don't eliminate it

ubicaciones.encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work

registros.texto: Accept that some shots will need re-rolls. Budget for it. The locks reduce the failure rate; they don't eliminate it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes

registros.texto: What goes wrong when generated images don't match the storyboard, and what to fix at the prompt level vs. accept as editorial work.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** plastic skin, oversaturated colors, eyes too symmetrical, hands wrong, generic stock-photo composition, lighting that's too even, "rendered" feel.

**Causes:**
- Generic mood adjectives ("beautiful", "stunning", "amazing")
- Stable Diffusion crutches ("4k", "highly detailed", "masterpiece") in non-SD generators
- Missing photographic specifics
- No "never" list applied from brand-lock

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Add specific lens and aperture ("50mm prime, f/2.0")
- Add film stock or camera reference ("Sony FX6", "Kodak Portra 400 film stock")
- Add "natural skin texture, no AI rendering artifacts" closing line (Flux, GPT Image)
- Verify brand-lock "never" list is being applied, if it includes "no AI uncanny", surface that into the prompt
- Use Flux 2 Pro or Midjourney v7 instead of cheaper models for hero shots

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** the brief is for stylized content where realism isn't the goal.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** same person looks different in shot 1 vs shot 5; clothing changes; hair color shifts; age perceived differently.

**Causes:**
- Series_lock character string paraphrased rather than verbatim
- No reference image passed (`--cref`, omni-reference)
- Seed not locked
- Too few features described in character anchor (gives generator too much room)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Verify character string is verbatim across every prompt
- Add 1–2 more specific features ("small scar above left eyebrow", "black wireframe glasses")
- Use reference image after the first successful shot
- Lock seed at storyboard level
- For Midjourney, use `--cref` with `--cw 50`

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** character consistency is genuinely impossible to lock. Budget re-rolls, typically 2–3× per problematic shot.
